quote: Twenty-four concurrent-flow tests were performed, focusing on finding flammability limits as a function of oxygen and flow speed.
statement: Number of concurrent rod tests performed (not analysed): 24. Figure 4 plots a subset of points. The same sentence repeats on p.2 and p.9.

quote: For blowoff limit tests, the astronaut quickly turned up the flow to obtain extinction.
statement: Blowoff protocol: flow turned up quickly until extinction.

quote: For quenching tests, the flow was incrementally turned down and the flame allowed to stabilize at the new flow condition for at least the solid-phase response time before changing it again.
statement: Quench protocol: flow stepped down with stabilization at each step (repeated on p.4 and p.9).

quote: Twenty-two rods were clear, and two were black, but no obvious differences between clear and black have been noted to date.
statement: Of the 24 tests, 22 clear rods and 2 black rods.

quote: Seventeen clear cast PMMA cylindrical rods of various diameters (11with 1/4”, 4 with 3/8”, and 2 with 1/2” diameters) were burned in a concurrent flow direction.
statement: 17 clear rod samples (counts per diameter); samples, not tests (some samples were reburned).

quote: The air velocity transducer probe had a response time of approximately one minute.
statement: Flow sensor response time ~1 min; p.2-3 continue: 'The fan voltage was calibrated with the air velocity transducer reading at the end of every operations day using that day's flow restrictor configuration(s).'

quote: Oxygen concentrations in the MSG working volume were varied during the testing from ambient ISS oxygen levels (~ 21% O2) down to ~14% O2
statement: Oxygen range of the tests: ~21% down to ~14% O2 (repeated in Conclusions, p.9).

quote: Quench test burns lasted up to 28 minutes.
The flow at blowoff was defined by the fan voltage reading at the moment the stagnation region opened up and the flame moved downstream.
statement: Blowoff flow comes from the fan voltage reading (via calibration), not from the Air display.

quote: the flame is unable to propagate upstream for the low oxygen levels tested (16.1% O2 and lower).
statement: Authors' hedged inference ('so it seems that'): once blown downstream, the flame appeared unable to propagate upstream and re-establish the stagnation region at the O2 levels tested, 16.1% O2 and lower. The paper reports one success, where the blowoff may have been incomplete.

quote: For each test, the flow at which the flames extinguished and the last flow where a stable flame was observed (or where the flame did not blowout in the drop time for drop tests), along with the post-burn oxygen reading were used to generate the flammability boundary, shown in Figure 4.
statement: Boundary points = extinction flow and last stable flow per test, with post-burn (final) O2.

Figure 4 legend text, read from the figure image (DERIVED_FROM_FIGURE): quench-branch fit; legend also reads 'Blowoff: 0.02x+13.3' and, for the drop-tower linear fit, 'y = 0.0181x + 13.42'. x axis 'Forced Stretch Rate, s-1', y axis 'Final O2 Concentration, % by volume'.

quote: Using the y-intercept of the linear fit (13.3 % O2 in the Figure 4 fit, versus the minimum test point of 13.6 % O2) would add a slight level of conservatism.
statement: Blowoff-branch y-intercept 13.3% O2; minimum test point 13.6% O2.

quote: The flow-induced stretch around the approximately spherical rod tip is af = 3/2 U/R.
statement: Forced stretch formula used for the Figure 4 x axis (R = rod radius, U = flow speed).

quote: Figure 4 currently shows the flammability boundary data plotted as forced stretch rate
statement: Figure 4 uses forced stretch only; curvature-induced stretch not yet included.
Rod radii (Figure 2 caption): R is radius, half of the 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 inch diameters.
